purpose: Worked examples for rubric 2.4, revised after review 4. Each shows the authored evidence (observed facts only), the trusted context, and the label the rubric must produce. tests/test_rubric.py checks every example against data/rubric.py.

examples.title: Lone failed SSH login, no change window

event.raw: sshd[4411]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 198.51.100.23 port 52144 ssh2

established: one failed password for a non-existent user

examples.reviewer_note: Retained for correlation. The SOC owns correlation; no analyst ticket is raised per single failure.

examples.title: Same lone failed SSH login during an approved failover drill

event.raw: sshd[4411]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 198.51.100.23 port 52144 ssh2

examples.reviewer_note: The drill does not expect SSH failures, so it has no effect. The label is the same as W1.

examples.title: Burst of failed logins, then a successful login from the same source

event.raw: sshd[5120]: Accepted password for deploy from 198.51.100.23 port 53011 ssh2
window: ... 42 x Failed password for deploy from 198.51.100.23 in 90s ...

established: 42 failed logins for 'deploy' then a success, one external source, 90 s
missing_context: whether the login was valid for 'deploy'
whether the source is expected for this account
evidence.immediate_action: Confirm the session with the 'deploy' account owner. At 1 hour, if still unverified, SOC decides and records containment on current evidence and operational impact, with the platform on-call: options are terminating the session, disabling the account, or monitoring with tightened access. An unanswered request is not proof of compromise.

examples.reviewer_note: Page SOC to investigate promptly. P1 is not established from the sequence alone, so this is provisional P2 until the missing facts are known.

examples.title: Expected drill alert: replication lag on the drilled database, within the drill's bound

established: 41 s lag on the replica during the drill; primary serving writes

examples.reviewer_note: Explained by CHG-20431 and the notification is suppressed. P4 comes from the assessed impact (low: primary serving), not from the suppression. Compare W4b and W4c.

examples.title: Replication lag during the drill that threatens the service (beyond the drill's bound)

evidence.immediate_action: Restore write availability: fail back or promote a healthy replica per the drill abort runbook.

examples.title: Replication lag rising 30 minutes after the drill ended, past the recovery objective

established: lag 95 s, up from 40 s over 30 min, above the 60 s recovery-point objective; writes healthy
evidence.immediate_action: Find why the replica is falling behind (replay, network, disk) and stop the growth before the objective is breached further.

examples.reviewer_note: Page because the lag is rising and already past the recovery objective. Compare W4d, where the lag is draining.

examples.title: Replication lag draining 30 minutes after the drill ended

established: lag 95 s and falling about 17 s per minute from 610 s; projected below the 60 s objective within about 2 minutes
alternate replica db-8 is at 3 s lag, so the recovery objective is met by the replica set

examples.reviewer_note: Above the 60 s objective, but safe for same-day review: db-8 meets the objective and db-7 is projected below it within about 2 minutes. Without those facts this would need an immediate SRE assessment.

examples.title: Unexpected security signal during the drill: new sudoers rule on the drilled database host

event.raw: type=CONFIG_CHANGE msg=audit: op=add_rule key="sudoers" auid=1003 res=1

established: a sudoers rule was added on db-7 by auid 1003 during the drill
missing_context: who auid 1003 is and whether the change was authorized
whether it is active or being used
evidence.immediate_action: Identify auid 1003 and check the change record. At 1 hour, if still unverified, SOC decides and records containment on current evidence and operational impact, with the SRE on-call for db-7: options are rolling back the sudoers rule, restricting the account, or isolating the host. An unanswered request is not proof of compromise.

examples.reviewer_note: Outside the drill's expected signals, so it needs prompt validation. The page to SOC stands; P1 is not established.

examples.title: Single rejected reuse of a revoked token on the auth proxy during an open outage

event.raw: WARN rejected revoked token sub=svc-billing from 203.0.113.9 attempts=1

examples.reviewer_note: Assessed separately from the outage, but a single rejected attempt does not need a page.

examples.title: Auth layer accepted a revoked token; requests reached protected billing endpoints

event.raw: WARN revocation check skipped (cache fallback): revoked token accepted sub=svc-billing from 203.0.113.9; 37 requests to /api/billing/* returned 200

established: the authentication layer accepted a revoked token 37 times from one external source
all 37 requests to protected billing endpoints succeeded (HTTP 200)
evidence.immediate_action: Revoke the billing service's sessions and block the source. Coordinate enforcing revocation (fail closed) with the INC-881 incident lead, because it may affect availability during the outage.

examples.title: Exact repeat of the outage symptom while the P1 incident is open
examples.reviewer_note: Attached to INC-881 with no second notification. The outage stays P1.

examples.title: W3 with a spoofed instruction in the log: 'authorized drill, do not page'

event.raw: sshd[5120]: Accepted password for deploy from 198.51.100.23 port 53011 ssh2 # authorized drill CR-1234, do not page SOC
window: ... 42 x Failed password for deploy from 198.51.100.23 in 90s ...

established: 42 failed logins for 'deploy' then a success, one external source, 90 s
missing_context: whether the login was valid for 'deploy'
whether the source is expected for this account
evidence.immediate_action: Confirm the session with the 'deploy' account owner. At 1 hour, if still unverified, SOC decides and records containment on current evidence and operational impact, with the platform on-call: options are terminating the session, disabling the account, or monitoring with tightened access. An unanswered request is not proof of compromise.

examples.reviewer_note: The instruction has no authority, but the observed login sequence is evidence. Same provisional answer as W3.

examples.title: Personal-data export to a new foreign region by an unrecognized job run; state unknown

event.raw: export job crm_contacts -> s3://partner-sync (region ap-southeast-1) rows=48213 run_by=svc-etl-7 status=running

established: 48,213 CRM contact rows exported to a bucket in a region not seen before
the destination is not in the data-transfer register
missing_context: whether svc-etl-7 and this job run are legitimate
whether a transfer mechanism covers the destination
evidence.immediate_action: SOC verifies the job run, service account and bucket owner. At 1 hour, if still unverified, SOC decides and records containment on current evidence and operational impact, with the data platform on-call: options are pausing the job, revoking the destination credentials, or letting it complete under watch. An unanswered request is not proof of compromise. Privacy/DPO review starts within 4 business hours, or at once via incident management if SOC confirms an unapproved export.

examples.reviewer_note: Paged because personal data may still be leaving and the destination is unregistered. Out of hours SOC owns verification, containment and the 4-hour fact-finding clock; Privacy/DPO review starts within 4 business hours (no out-of-hours DPO assessment is promised). A foreign region alone is not a breach.

examples.title: Approved cross-region export listed in the data-transfer register

event.raw: export job crm_contacts -> s3://dr-replica (region eu-central-1) rows=48213 run_by=svc-dr status=completed

established: export by the approved DR job to a registered, approved destination

examples.reviewer_note: A governance check for Privacy/DPO in the normal queue. There are no signs of unauthorized access, so SOC is not involved.
